profile.summary: TREDNet predicts whether a 2,000 base pair stretch of human DNA acts as an enhancer, and how much a single-nucleotide variant changes that prediction. It works in two stages: a first convolutional network turns the one-hot encoded sequence into 1,924 predicted epigenomic signals (DNase I hypersensitivity, histone modifications and transcription factor binding), and a second, smaller network turns that vector into an enhancer probability for one tissue or cell line. Released phase two models cover pancreatic islets, HepG2 and K562.

summary_quotes.text: we developed TREDNet, a two-phase DL framework consisting of two consecutive convolutional neural networks (CNNs): the first to predict epigenomic signals across the genome and the second to predict enhancers
we trained a CNN that uses tiled DNA sequences of 2,000 base pairs (bp) to predict DNase I hypersensitive sites (DHSs), histone modifications (HMs), and TF-binding sites (TFBSs)
The result of this two-phase learning framework is the enhancer probability of a 2,000 bp DNA sequence.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Phase one is a multitask convolutional classifier in the style of DeepSEA, Beluga and DanQ. It takes a one-hot encoded 2,000 base window and outputs 1,924 values, one per epigenomic feature. Phase two is a smaller convolutional network trained on enhancer regions, but each region is first passed through phase one and so is represented by the 1,924-value vector rather than by its sequence. Phase two can be a single-output classifier for one tissue or a multitask classifier over several. Chromosomes 8 and 9 were held out of training and used for testing.

quotes.text: It predicts 1924 genomic features of transcription factors, histone modifications and DNase-I Hypersensitivity Sites
each region is first passed through the first phase and converted to a vector of length 1924
The model can be built as a single output classifier (enhancers of a single tissue) or multitask classifier (enhancers of multiple tissues)
We excluded signals on chromosomes 8 and 9 from training and used them to test the model’s accuracy.

sections.title: Scoring variants and regions
sections.body: The repository's score_variant.py reads a VCF, needs an hg19 FASTA, and writes a tab-separated file. With -score-iep it builds the 2,000 base reference and alternate sequences centred on the SNP, predicts both, and scores the variant as the larger probability times the absolute difference between the two. With -score-delta it takes the 2,000 base window around the variant, substitutes every other base at each position from 990 to 1010, averages the drop from the reference prediction at each position and divides by the median absolute value, writing the resulting list of values. Separately, the paper reports saturated mutagenesis across whole enhancers, which it calls enhancer damage (ED) scores, and defines peaks and dips in them as enhancer damaging regions (EDRs) and enhancer strengthening regions (ESRs). A second module, peak_detection/annotate.py, performs what the README calls PAS/DAS detection from a file of precomputed deltas.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Four weight files are released on Zenodo record 6463875: one phase one model and three phase two models (islets, HepG2, K562). The same weights are registered in the Kipoi database, where each entry pins the weight URL and an MD5 checksum. The Kipoi entries declare python 3.9 with keras 2.8 and tensorflow 2.8, while the repository's requirements.txt pins keras 2.1.2 and tensorflow 1.4.1, so a result should say which route and which versions were used, along with the phase two cell name.

facts.value: Not reported. The sources read give no parameter counts. For scale, the released weight files are about 575 MB (phase one) and about 148 MB each (phase two).

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Phase one: DNase I hypersensitive sites, histone modifications and TF binding sites across 127 human cell types and tissues from ENCODE and NIH Roadmap, 1,924 features in total (the README says 123 tissues and cell lines). Phase two: islet enhancers defined from ATAC-seq peaks and H3K27ac marks, and HepG2 and K562 enhancers. Chromosomes 8 and 9 were withheld. The Kipoi model descriptions instead say chromosomes 7, 8 and 9 were held out.

gaps: No parameter counts, layer sizes or filter widths are given in the sources read; the paper's Methods are in the supplementary appendix, which was not fetched.
The weights licence is stated differently by Zenodo (CC BY 4.0) and by the repository's Kipoi descriptions (CC-BY-ND).
The README's hg19 FASTA download URL is missing (the sentence ends before the link).
The Kipoi entries cite a medRxiv preprint, while the README cites the published PNAS paper read here.
The held-out chromosomes disagree: the paper says 8 and 9, the Kipoi descriptions say 7, 8 and 9.
The paper describes ED scores, EDRs and ESRs across whole enhancers, while score_variant.py computes Delta values over a 21-position window around a variant; no source read states how the two relate.

run_guide.summary: Get the repository at the pinned commit, install its dependencies, download the four weight files and score variants from a VCF with the islet phase two model.
prerequisites: Python with keras and tensorflow. The repository's requirements.txt pins keras 2.1.2 and tensorflow 1.4.1; the Kipoi route declares python 3.9 with keras 2.8 and tensorflow 2.8.
The GRCh37/hg19 human genome FASTA file. The README names it but its download URL is missing from the README.
A GPU is recommended but not required for predictions. Training from scratch needs a CUDA Linux machine with more than 150 GB of memory.
About 1 GB of download for the four weight files. Code is MIT licensed; the Zenodo record is CC BY 4.0.

notes: The repository also holds a newer line of work (train_phase_one_plain*.py, peak_detection/) and other groups publish TREDNet variants (NLM-DIR/Shift-Aware-TREDNetV2, tanoManzo/TREDNET_v2); only the okurman/TREDNet release is described here. The weights licence conflicts between Zenodo (CC BY 4.0) and the repository's Kipoi descriptions (CC-BY-ND), which is worth a human check. The README's feature-coverage figure (123 tissues and cell lines) differs from the paper's (127 cell types and tissues); both are quoted. The existing source regulatory-variant-20261009-source-manzo2025 is the comparison paper, not the model's own documentation. The held-out chromosomes also differ between the paper (8 and 9) and the Kipoi descriptions (7, 8 and 9).
